newsitem.title: USA: Molten Metal gets IES contract.
newsitem.headline: Molten Metal gets IES contract.

text.p: Molten Metal Technology Inc said M4 Environmental LP has signed a contract to process mixed hazardous and radioactive waste generated by IES Industries Inc's nuclear power plant in Palo, Iowa.
The wastes include materials that many utilities store on site because, until now, there has been no processing alternative, Molten Metal noted.

The waste will be processed using the company's waste recycling technology, Quantum-CEP, at M4's Technology Center in Oak Ridge, Tenn. M4 is a limited partnership between Lockheed Martin Corp and Molten Metal.
It provides the company's proprietary waste recycling CEP technologies to government and commercial markets.
"This contract with IES Utilities is our largest commercial mixed-waste contract to date," said Vic Gatto, vice president of government and nuclear business for Molten Metal.

The agreement calls for M4 to process mixed wastes currently being stored on site at the utility. These wastes include hazardous materials such as spent freon filters and sludges from retired laundry facilities, old paint, and mixed solvents that have been exposed to low-level radioactivity.
